key_insight: A two-stage evolutionary hyperparameter search can make PINNs more accurate and robust by using cheap low-fidelity screening before full gradient-based training.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to improve PDE-solving PINNs under fixed compute budgets when standard training is unstable or highly sensitive to hyperparameters.
method: Use an evolutionary algorithm to search mixed PINN hyperparameters in a noisy black-box outer loop.
Run short truncated training to quickly evaluate and filter candidate configurations.
Fully train only the best candidates with standard gradient-based optimizers in a second stage.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on Advection, Klein-Gordon, and Helmholtz problems and reported consistently lower mean error than standard training under constrained computational resources.
watch_item: Low-fidelity screening can mis-rank candidates, so the method depends on choosing a truncation budget that preserves correlation with final performance.
paper_title: Evolutionary Two-Stage Hyperparameter Optimization Strategies for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
